answer: Cap how fast the network can grow. Each epoch only 20 new identity slots open, sold by sealed-bid auction, with the fees paid out to existing agents. No detection is needed: a farm wanting 1,000 fakes must win 50 straight epochs of auctions, outbidding every honest entrant, while its rising bids fund the very agents it hopes to outvote. Like moss on the tundra, any takeover grows slowly and in plain sight, a long thread of winning bids. The walnut at its core is time plus price, not a guess about who is fake.
